To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

4E-BPs negatively regulate cell cycle progression and survival in response to hypoxia, and that 4EBP1 knockdown in Rh30 cells results in increased cyclin D1, c-Myc, and antiapoptotic gene expression and increased mitotic aberrations in vivo.
4E-BPs negatively regulate the eIF4E activity that is required for cell division and survival under hypoxic stress conditions, and that this activity is essential for tumor growth.
reduced 4E-BPs expression enhances tumor cell proliferation and viability in response to hypoxia, and this may be due in part to increased expression of cyclins and antiapoptotic factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the translational machinery in cancer progression.
the role of the translational machinery in regulating cell cycle progression in hypoxic tumor microenvironment.
the role of the eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E binding protein 1 (4E-BP) and its regulation by the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) in cancer progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our data suggest that 4E-BPs are important regulators of cell cycle progression and tumor growth, and that the hypoxic tumor microenvironment is an important regulator of 4E-binding protein expression.
our data support the hypothesis that eIF4F plays a key role in regulating cell division, proliferation, and survival in hypoxic tumors.
4E-BPs are critical regulators of cell division, and their loss may be associated with increased cell proliferation and survival in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

4E-BPs play a role in regulating cell cycle progression and cell death in response to hypoxic conditions, and that the eIF4E/eIF4G complex is required for hypoxic inhibition of cell cycle progression and survival.
4E-BPs are important regulators of tumor cell survival and proliferation under hypoxic conditions and that 4E-E-BP1 may be an important therapeutic target in the context of tumor hypoxia.
eIF4F activation is a potential therapeutic target for cancer treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
4E-BPs play a critical role in regulating the response to hypoxia and the progression of tumors.
the eIF4E/eIF4E-BP complex may be a useful therapeutic target in the context of hypoxic tumors.

4E-BPs are not just inhibitors of eIF4e, but are also involved in cell cycle progression, and that the effects of eIF4f on tumor cell proliferation and viability are complex and depend on the context.
